basic_identification.full_title: Specification for Flake Resins for Use in Shell Process in Foundries
basic_identification.sector_category: Structural and Metals / Foundry and Castings (approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council and finalized by the Foundry Sectional Committee of the Indian Standards Institution)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements for flake resin, catalyst, and lubricant in combination, intended for use in the production of shell cores or moulds using the hot sand coating process in foundries.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Unlike builders hardware or metal packaging containers which are subject to mandatory statutory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), industrial flake resins for use in foundries are certified on a voluntary basis. Manufacturers who consistently meet the criteria may apply for a license to apply the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to their packaging. Compliance with this standard is typically a mandatory technical requirement inside public, railway, and private sector foundry raw material procurement tenders.

requirements.detail: The flake resin must be synthetic in nature, produced by the catalytic reaction of phenol and formaldehyde, representing a novolak (novolac) type resin suitable for the hot coating of sand.
The resin must be supplied specifically in the form of flakes of uniform quality.
The catalyst required for resin curing (hot-coating chemical action) must be manufactured by pulverizing hexamine powder.
A lubricant consisting of wax and specialized additives may be added separately into the sand mix during the coating operation.

requirements.requirement_type: Grade Classification based on Melting Point
requirements.detail: The flake resins are classified into two distinct functional grades depending on their melting points: Grade I and Grade II.

Sampling and physical testing must be carried out according to the manufacturer's production batches. A suitable sized sample must be drawn from all the drums of a particular batch, mixed thoroughly, and used for testing.

The physical dimensions of the resin flakes (length, width, and thickness in millimetres) are strictly specified under Table 1 of the standard to ensure uniform melting and distribution during hot coating.

A sand mix prepared with 3.5% flake resin on sand and 15% catalyst on flake resin must satisfy strict physical requirements specified under Table 1, including cold tensile strength, stick point, and gas content.
Each drum or bag of product must carry the name of the product, date of manufacture, expiry date, and the production batch number.
Conforming products may be marked with the ISI Certification Mark on their containers as a further assurance of quality.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11266 : 1985 is the national Indian Standard specification governing flake resins (novolac phenol-formaldehyde synthetic resins) utilized alongside hexamine catalysts and wax lubricants in hot-coating sand processes in foundries. This process produces high-strength, dimensionally accurate shell cores and moulds. Certified on a voluntary basis under the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) scheme, the standard classifies resins into Grade I and Grade II based on their melting points. It enforces rigorous batch-level quality controls, requiring that the raw flakes and the subsequently coated sand mixtures satisfy strict physical and mechanical benchmarks—including flake size dimensions, cold tensile strength, stick point, and evolved gas volume limits—to prevent core sagging, lumping, or casting blowhole defects.
